findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 59 mm is observed in the head of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the portal vein, suggesting invasion. No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum is observed. The tumor is also in contact with the right renal vein, which shows stenosis, indicating invasion. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastasis is observed in one node at station 8p. No other metastases are observed.

responses.content:

CH: 0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU: 0 (no invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum)
S: 1 (serosal invasion)
RP: 1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV: 1 (invasion of the portal vein)
A: 1 (invasion of the right renal vein)
PL: 0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO: 0 (no invasion of the omental vessels)

Task 1 response: CH0, DU0, S1, RP1, PV1, A1, PL0, OO0

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (59 mm), it is classified as T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the head are:
- Station 8p (left gastric artery lymph node)
- Station 8a (common hepatic artery lymph node)
- Station 12a (proper hepatic artery lymph node)
- Station 12b (gastroduodenal artery lymph node)
- Station 12p (common bile duct lymph node)

The patient's metastatic lymph node station is:
- Station 8p

This is a regional lymph node, so the N classification is N1a.

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

There are no distant metastases, so the M classification is M0.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the local invasion factors, the tumor is not unresectable. There is no evidence of distant or non-regional metastasis, so the tumor is resectable.

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

T classification: T3
N classification: N1a
M classification: M0

Based on the T classification, the tumor is classified as Stage III.
